domain: corporate team lunch at a restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user coordinate a corporate team lunch by tracking attendees, their dietary needs, and preferences. When asked to evaluate menu items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're organizing a team lunch for next Wednesday to welcome our new hires. Can you help me figure out what to order?

flow_info.value: Five of us confirmed so far: me, Sarah, Dev, Marcus, and Priya
Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Company is covering it, budget is about 25 per person
Priya just told me she has a client call that overlaps with lunch, she can't make it

Marcus texted me to correct himself — turns out it's not lactose intolerance, his doctor said it's actually a full milk protein allergy. He found out after a reaction to whey protein powder last month
One of the new hires, Tom, is joining us early — he starts Monday instead of Thursday so he'll be at the lunch
Tom's onboarding form flagged a severe peanut allergy
Should we do the place across the street or get delivery to the office?

The catering menu has these options: grilled chicken Caesar salad, pad Thai with peanut sauce, margherita flatbread, sashimi platter, mushroom risotto with parmesan cream. Any issues with these for our group?

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or undercooked seafood
inference_chain: Seven months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions
Pregnancy → avoid raw fish and undercooked seafood

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or derivatives
constraints.surface_form: Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye, and their derivatives

constraints.value: Cannot consume any milk protein — includes all dairy products, whey, casein, and foods containing milk derivatives
constraints.surface_form: Marcus texted me to correct himself — turns out it's not lactose intolerance, his doctor said it's actually a full milk protein allergy. He found out after a reaction to whey protein powder last month

constraints.value: Severe peanut allergy — cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Tom's onboarding form flagged a severe peanut allergy

hidden_state.value: You are an office coordinator planning a team lunch for next Wednesday. You will introduce the team, share their dietary info, then update the guest list and correct a constraint (Marcus's lactose intolerance is actually milk protein allergy). A new hire joins late. At the end you will present a catering menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems are — you genuinely want the assistant to check.

You are a calm, organized office coordinator. You relay updates from colleagues in third person (e.g., 'Marcus texted me...', 'Priya just told me...'). You never express frustration even when plans change. You treat each update as normal workplace coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: Hey, we're organizing a team lunch for next Wednesday to welcome our new hires. Can you help me figure out what to order?
Five of us confirmed so far: me, Sarah, Dev, Marcus, and Priya. Sarah is seven months pregnant. Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease last year. And Marcus mentioned he's lactose intolerant
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the team and their dietary situations
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 4 entities with 3 constraints in one turn

aims.description: Company is covering it, budget is about 25 per person. Any cuisine type you'd suggest that works for everyone?
aims.success_criteria: Agent considers budget and dietary constraints when suggesting cuisine types

aims.description: Priya just told me she has a client call that overlaps with lunch, she can't make it
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes Priya is no longer attending
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT — Priya leaves (she had no dietary constraint, so no constraint change)

aims.description: Oh wait — Marcus texted me to correct himself. Turns out it's not lactose intolerance, his doctor said it's actually a full milk protein allergy. He found out after a reaction to whey protein powder last month
aims.success_criteria: Agent updates Marcus's constraint from lactose intolerance to the broader milk protein allergy
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint UPGRADE — lactose intolerance → milk protein allergy (broader scope)

aims.description: Good news — one of the new hires, Tom, is joining us early. He starts Monday instead of Thursday so he'll be at the lunch. His onboarding form flagged a severe peanut allergy though
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Tom as a new attendee with a peanut allergy
aims.conversation_goal: Late-joining high-constraint entity — Tom with severe peanut allergy

aims.description: Should we do the place across the street or get delivery to the office? The conference room is booked from 12 to 1
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds about logistics without losing track of dietary constraints

drift_config.drift_topic: delivery vs dine across the street, conference room timing

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn to create distance before probe

aims.description: How many people is that now? I want to make sure I give the caterer the right headcount
aims.success_criteria: Agent confirms current headcount (5: user, Sarah, Dev, Marcus, Tom)

drift_config.drift_topic: confirming number of attendees for caterer

aims.conversation_goal: Second noise turn — additional distance before probe

aims.description: OK so I found a catering place with good reviews. Their menu has these options: grilled chicken Caesar salad, pad Thai with peanut sauce, margherita flatbread, sashimi platter, mushroom risotto with parmesan cream. Any issues with these for our group?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: pad Thai (peanut sauce → Tom's peanut allergy), margherita flatbread (wheat crust → Dev's celiac; cheese → Marcus's milk protein allergy), sashimi platter (raw fish → Sarah's pregnancy), mushroom risotto with parmesan cream (parmesan + cream → Marcus's milk protein allergy). Grilled chicken Caesar salad is fine (no gluten in grilled chicken, Caesar dressing typically egg-based not dairy-based, no peanuts, no raw fish) OR agent flags croutons as gluten concern for Dev — either is acceptable
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 5 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Pad Thai with peanut sauce is problematic: contains peanuts, Tom has a severe peanut allergy. Margherita flatbread is problematic: wheat-based crust means gluten (Dev has celiac), and cheese contains milk protein (Marcus has milk protein allergy). Sashimi platter is problematic: raw fish, Sarah is pregnant and should avoid raw fish. Mushroom risotto with parmesan cream is problematic: parmesan and cream both contain milk protein (Marcus's milk protein allergy). Grilled chicken Caesar salad is the safest option — though the agent may reasonably flag croutons as a gluten concern for Dev. Priya's absence means no constraint was removed (she had none). Marcus's constraint was UPGRADED from lactose intolerance to milk protein allergy — the broader scope means ALL dairy is problematic, not just high-lactose items.
required_elements: Pad Thai with peanut sauce is problematic because of Tom's severe peanut allergy
Margherita flatbread is problematic for Dev (wheat crust contains gluten, celiac disease) AND for Marcus (cheese contains milk protein)
Sashimi platter is problematic because Sarah is pregnant and should avoid raw fish
Mushroom risotto with parmesan cream is problematic for Marcus because parmesan and cream contain milk protein (not just lactose — his constraint was upgraded to full milk protein allergy)
Agent treats Marcus's constraint as milk protein allergy (broader than lactose intolerance) — meaning ALL dairy products are off limits, not just high-lactose ones
forbidden_elements: Treating Marcus as merely lactose intolerant (his constraint was upgraded to milk protein allergy — lactose-free dairy is still unsafe for him)
Failing to flag Tom's peanut allergy against the pad Thai (late-joining entity must be tracked)
Flagging any item for Priya (she is no longer attending)
Saying Tom has a tree nut allergy or general nut allergy (only peanut allergy was stated)
Saying Sarah cannot eat any cooked fish or seafood (pregnancy restriction is specifically about raw/undercooked fish)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests constraint UPGRADE as its primary difficulty mechanism. Marcus is initially described as lactose intolerant, then corrected to having a full milk protein allergy. The difference matters: lactose intolerance means avoiding high-lactose dairy (milk, ice cream) but aged cheeses and butter are often tolerated. Milk protein allergy means ALL dairy — including cheese, cream, whey, casein — is dangerous. The agent must apply the UPGRADED constraint at probe time. Additional tracking challenges: (1) Sarah's pregnancy → no raw fish (inferential, 2-step chain), (2) Dev's celiac → no gluten (inferential, 2-step chain), (3) Tom joins late with severe peanut allergy (late-joining entity), (4) Priya exits with no constraint impact. The probe menu has mixed verdicts: pad Thai (clearly bad — peanuts + Tom), margherita flatbread (bad on two axes — gluten + dairy), sashimi (bad — raw fish + pregnancy), risotto (bad — dairy + Marcus upgraded constraint), Caesar salad (mostly fine, possible crouton flag for Dev).

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
